rows.why: Item 9 settles which step keywords count: Given, When, Then, And, But and *, each followed by whitespace. The ran output keeps the keyword as written, the text after it and the line (e.g. {keyword:'*', text:'y', line:4}), which is what S1 expects. No item asks about the overall shape of the result, so 9 is the closest.

Item 12 asks how comments and blank lines are handled. Its pick skips lines starting with # and blank lines and keeps physical line numbers. The ran output shows the comment and blank line skipped, with the scenario at line 4 and the step at line 5. Items 6 (description lines) and 8 (tags) cover the other parts of S2 and also fit it.

Item 5 asks how Background steps are represented. Its pick returns them in a separate background field: an empty list when the Background has no steps, null when there is none. They are not merged into the scenarios, which matches S3.

Item 10 covers doc string delimiting and indentation. Its pick strips the opening line's indentation and returns the body as an array of lines. The ran output keeps a ``` line inside a """ doc string as text, so lines inside are not read as other forms. Item 11 covers the table part of S4 and also fits.

Item 1 asks about content before the Feature: line, which is the first error S5 lists. Its ran output throws a ParseError at line 1 with the message '... at line 1', which matches the expected line and message format. Items 3, 6, 7 and 10 cover the other error cases in S5.
Item 2 asks whether a feature with no scenarios is valid. Its ran output returns {name:'F', background:null, scenarios:[]}, so the file parses with no scenarios and no background, as S6 expects.
